title: Test The Plan With The Team
objective: Test a real project step with collaborators, agree a practical change and record your own part in that decision.

blocks.text: GROW · Art · Week 5. Trinity Arts Award Silver. Test The Plan With The Team.
Objective: Test a real project step with collaborators, agree a practical change and record your own part in that decision.
Success evidence: the actual team test, other people’s responses, your contribution and an updated practical plan with exact evidence locations.
Unit 2 is your arts leadership project. Keep it distinct from your personal arts challenge in Unit 1. These lessons support your real project at its planned scale.
40-minute lesson frame. Real activity may continue in recorded programme time. No event, attendance or booking is asserted here.

This deck directly serves Silver Unit 2, Arts leadership, Parts 2B and 2D. Part 2B requires planning promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. This session tests and updates the existing practical plan. Part 2D requires working effectively with others. Preserve the pupil’s own contribution, actual exchanges and response to collaborators. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Silver has TWO units, evidenced separately: Unit 1 Arts practice and pathways; Unit 2 Arts leadership. Mark P / A / N per part. ONE Attempted is allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass / Below Pass only. The whole Silver portfolio has a 20-file cap across both units, not twenty per unit. Organise evidence by unit and part. Nine cumulative part files or two clearly sectioned unit files are optional layouts. Name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode for each item. One real record may support two parts with clear locators; do not count duplicate copies as extra evidence. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Confirm these locally, not as an accomplished fact in this deck. Adults may scribe exact pupil words or confirmed signs and check them back, but must not write the pupil’s plan, review or evidence. Staff may separately record factual observations. Core, Extend and Challenge are support choices within Silver and retain the actual role, contribution and evidence. No public showing is imposed as a Silver requirement. Fourteen forty-minute sessions do not supply all 95 programme hours; record actual further guided and independent time.

Retrieve each pupil’s 2A role and 2B practical plan. Arrange available collaborators, including staff where appropriate. Prepare actual project materials or safe substitutes for the rehearsal, plus blank paper. For the teacher model use a pencil, paper and a clear instruction card made on the board. Check permission, access, materials and local risk arrangements before any trial. The practical test and collaboration can evidence 2B and 2D, but must not be relabelled as completed project delivery. If real collaborators or materials are unavailable, retain preparation honestly and arrange the missing practical test. Do not supply a ready-written pupil plan.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Check actual plans and roles; help retrieve missing work without filling its choices for the pupil.

blocks.text: Open your purpose, role and plan. Identify your next responsibility and what others need from you.
Check promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback: how people hear, who joins, tools, possible harm and responses.
Test a safe step with available people and time. A useful problem can show what needs changing.
Keep the original plan so the update can be compared.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Write the full example on the board. It is a teaching case, not a claim about the pupil’s project.

blocks.text: Read this teacher example: the instruction says, Make a pattern with three types of mark. The pencil and paper are ready, but the group cannot see an example of a mark.
What would you check before deciding the group needs more pencils? The missing help may be a clear explanation, not another resource.
A plan can look complete on paper yet leave a person unsure what to do. Testing lets a real person try the step and describe what happened. Guessing what they might think does not do that job.

Each collaborator may notice something different. One may need the instruction closer. Another may need more time. A useful test makes room for their actual response rather than asking them to agree that your plan is good.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Run the short demonstration with a real willing colleague or pupil. Preserve their actual response; if it differs from the example, model that difference honestly.

blocks.text: Watch the adult model a small test with a willing partner. They show paper and a pencil and ask the partner to make a pattern using three types of mark.
The partner says what is clear and what needs explaining. The adult listens without finishing the reply. They repeat the point back: You want to see what counts as a type of mark. Is that right?
The adult then draws a dot, a short line and a curve on scrap paper. They name the actions while making them. They ask whether this makes the instruction clearer, rather than claiming it must help.
They agree a change together: keep a large mark example beside the task. The adult records the real response and the change to this model test. Your test may need a different change.

Notice the sequence. We tried the instruction first, heard a response, checked its meaning, then agreed what to change. The adult did not invent a complaint or write the partner’s answer before asking.
If the test reveals a safety issue, stop that part and involve the responsible adult. Agreement between pupils does not make unsafe equipment safe.

blocks.title: Test a plan with real people
blocks.caption: A practical change grows from a real test.
blocks.alt: Test a plan with real people. TRY a safe project step. LISTEN hear the real response. AGREE choose an action. UPDATE record what changed. A practical change grows from a real test.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Read the actual prompt and choices; support the pupil to commit before checking. Use the item feedback as a model reason, not a judgement on personal taste. Keep real trials, meetings, views and project actions separate from these teaching examples.

data.heading: Predict a clearer instruction, then ask
data.instruction: Predict before a willing collaborator tries the instruction. Keep the original. Check the actual response without supplying it for them.

items.label: The wording and viewing place stay the same, but the letters become larger. What is a fair prediction?
items.feedback: Larger letters may be easier to see. The collaborator’s actual response tests the prediction; size alone does not ensure understanding.

options.label: The larger letters may be clearer from that place.
The larger letters must solve every access difficulty.

items.label: The collaborator says both versions are already clear. What does the trial show?
items.feedback: Keep the true response. You do not need to manufacture a problem or claim an improvement that was not observed.

options.label: The larger version improved it, regardless of their reply.
This person found both versions clear in this trial.

items.label: You change the words, letter size and position together. What can you conclude?
items.feedback: A combined change may help the task, but the test does not isolate letter size. Explain the limit when updating the plan.

options.label: We must check the whole change and cannot isolate letter size.
Any improvement proves letter size alone caused it.

data.discussion: Test an actual project step with the team. Agree the action and your own contribution. Keep rehearsal and preparation distinct from real delivery.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Point to the actual model test and its update. Identify 2B and 2D separately without requiring duplicate evidence files.

blocks.text: Compare two teaching notes: “We sorted it” and “I showed the instruction; my partner tested it; I checked their reply and enlarged the example.” The second identifies roles, but it must also be true.
Name your action and the other person’s contribution. The updated plan supports 2B; the exchange supports 2D. They can share a file with distinct locations.

Recheck resources, risk, space, recruitment and feedback after a change. A larger display may need more space. A shorter task changes the invitation and timing; ask the people involved before claiming agreement.
Keep the original and update. Mark untested parts: one successful trial cannot settle every issue.

blocks.title: A plan change and a team contribution

boxes.head: PRACTICAL PLAN
boxes.line2: why the test led to it

blocks.caption: Keep both meanings clear in the same real record.
blocks.alt: A plan change and a team contribution. PRACTICAL PLAN what we changed why the test led to it. WORKING TOGETHER what I contributed how I responded to others. Keep both meanings clear in the same real record.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Facilitate a real exchange; do not substitute a fictional partner or claim rehearsal as delivery. Allow more programme time if the chosen test needs it.

blocks.text: Now choose one step from your own plan to test with a real collaborator. Tell them what you want to find out and invite them to try it. Use agreed safe materials.
Watch what happens before offering an answer. Ask what helped or got in the way. Check their meaning by repeating or showing the point back.
Agree one action to keep, change or check further. You may disagree at first. Give a reason tied to the task, and ask for the other person’s reason before deciding.

Record the trial while the details are fresh. Label it preparation or rehearsal. This actual team test supports planning and working together; it is not a claim that your whole project has been delivered.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Every tier retains an actual practical test, collaboration and pupil-authored update. Scribe exact words and confirm them; do not write the decision.

blocks.text: Use the test result to update your practical plan. Show what changed and why, or explain why you kept a step. Check promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback for any linked change.
Agree who will carry out the next action. State your own part clearly, alongside any part another person has accepted. Do not assign a job to someone who has not agreed to it.
Keep the other person’s response accurately, then record your own contribution and how you responded. Ask them to check a shared factual detail if needed; your explanation remains yours.
Core: use the five practical headings and help with materials. Take your own part in the real test, listen and agree an action. Dictate or show your update and contribution for an accurate record.
Extend: conduct the test, agree the practical action and update your plan. Link your own contribution and the response from others to the decision you made.
Challenge: retain the same real test and records. Check a consequence of the change elsewhere in the plan and agree how the team will handle it.

Save the records under Unit 2, Parts 2B and 2D. Name the actual file and page, slide or timecode for each. If a test could not happen, name what remains to be done rather than reporting an imagined outcome.

stages.title: Exit · check the next action
stages.data-ta1: Check the saved locators and actual readiness. Keep unresolved practical tasks open; do not infer delivery from preparation.

blocks.text: Show your collaborator the updated step and your own next job. Ask whether the record matches the action you agreed. Correct a factual error without changing someone’s words to make them sound more helpful.
Use the file location to find the first plan, the trial and the update. Can a reader tell what you did, what another person contributed and why the decision changed?
The next session supports real delivery when the project is ready. Keep any missing permission, resource or agreement visible. A plan being saved does not mean those jobs are complete.

print.intro: Test a real step with collaborators. Keep the true response, your agreed practical update and your own part in the exchange.
focusRows: Which step did we actually test, and with whom?
What response did I hear, and how did I check it?
What did I contribute, what changed, and who agreed the next action?
tiers: Core: use the five practical headings and help with materials. Take your own part in the real test, listen and agree an action. Dictate or show your update and contribution for an accurate record.
Extend: conduct the test, agree the practical action and update your plan. Link your own contribution and the response from others to the decision you made.
Challenge: retain the same real test and records. Check a consequence of the change elsewhere in the plan and agree how the team will handle it.
checks: A real safe test occurred, or the missing test is honestly named.
The update checks promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback as relevant.
My own contribution and response to collaborators are identifiable.
Preparation is not falsely claimed as project delivery.
Unit 2 Parts 2B and 2D have actual file-plus-page, slide or timecode locators.
